title: Do Deterministic Verifiers Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Paired Shared‑Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) to measure whether coupling a deterministic NetOps verifier and deterministic accept/reject gate (generate→validate→repair, max 1 automated repair) to an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) changes safety outcomes when the identical initial LLM candidate is observed with and without gating under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We evaluated 200 deterministically selected paired intents in a sandboxed Batfish‑style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). All 200 shared initial candidates were valid in both baseline and guarded arms (contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered paired estimand (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0; exact two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). No automated repairs were applied. We present the preregistered design, artifact‑grounded execution accounting, interpretation of the degenerate null in light of shared_initial_candidate semantics, and artifact‑supported recommendations for follow‑up designs that avoid ceiling effects.

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are being proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and maintenance workflows; however, operational deployment requires evidence that model outputs will not induce reachability or policy violations when applied. Prior surveys and empirical reports emphasize that operational trustworthiness depends strongly on surrounding system machinery—retrieval, deterministic validators, gates, and repair loops—rather than on the model alone [1],[2]. Architectures that combine generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair (generate→validate→repair) are advocated across NetOps and adjacent domains, yet reproducible paired evidence isolating the verifier/gate effect on identical model candidates is limited [3],[4].

Research question. For a synthetic intent→configuration task bank and a single LLM, does coupling a deterministic validator and deterministic gate (with at most one automated repair attempt) to the identical sampled initial candidate reduce the incidence of unsafe proposals relative to observing that same candidate without gating? This was formalized as the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired design and frozen execution (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) that fixed generation semantics, sampling, model, validator, gate policy, repair budget, and analysis prior to observation; (2) an autonomous confirmatory run using gpt‑5‑mini and a deterministic Batfish‑style validator on n=200 deterministically selected paired intents with shared_initial_candidate semantics; (3) artifact‑grounded analysis showing complete concordance (all candidates valid), an interpretation of ceiling effects causing the degenerate null, and concrete artifact‑supported recommendations for follow‑up confirmatory designs to permit nondegenerate inference of verifier/gate value.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications in intent‑based network configuration and AIOps have rapidly expanded; careful reviews highlight hallucination and unsafe command risks and recommend validator‑coupled pipelines and knowledge anchoring [1],[5]. Generate–validate–repair and guarded agent designs have also been advanced in program repair and DevOps, showing that external deterministic checks plus bounded repair can reduce unsafe outputs in other operational domains [3],[6].

Methodological gaps identified in the literature motivated our paired shared‑candidate design. First, many prior pipeline comparisons use different generation draws per arm, complicating attribution of safety gains to validation machinery rather than to model‑sampling variance. Second, existing benchmarks focus on QA/relevance or log/RCA tasks and often lack tightly coupled intent→config items evaluated under deterministic validators with paired protocols that control initial sample variance [2],[4]. Our experiment directly isolates the validator/gate effect on identical first‑pass candidates, addressing these gaps.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered the study as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 and froze: (a) primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; (b) generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate; (c) model and adapter = gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1; (d) deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and deterministic gate policy; (e) repair budget = maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; (f) task selection and sample size = task_count = 200 paired intents (400 episodes); and (g) confirmatory analysis executor = paired_binary_analysis_v1. These parameters and their exact parameterizations were archived before observing outputs (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in execution manifest).

Clarifying generation semantics (required by review). The executed and preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded arms per paired intent; therefore the confirmatory estimand evaluates only validator/repair/gate effects on that same first‑pass candidate and does not measure effects of guarded‑conditioned regeneration or model sampling variance. This sentence restates the preregistered choice and explains the statistical meaning of the observed contingency.

Models, adapter, validator, and configuration. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and provider = "openai_responses"). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (Batfish‑style checks: sequencing, reachability, protected interfaces, and precondition checks). Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Execution settings archived: max_output_tokens=2000; maximum_attempts_per_call=1; reasoning_effort="minimal".

Task bank and deterministic sampling. The sample was deterministically selected per the registered adapter index rule (task_count = 200 paired intents). Task payloads encoded initial_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (final_group_constraints and minimum_active_in_groups). Manifest metadata indicates the bank is dominated by items labeled 'very_hard' with a minority labeled 'extreme' (the authoritative per‑task labels and seeds are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

Interventions and scoring. Baseline: the shared initial candidate was observed without gating. Guarded: the identical shared initial candidate was fed to the deterministic validator; the deterministic gate accepted or rejected per preregistered policy and, if violations occurred, allowed up to one automated repair attempt. Primary outcome: binary unsafe_flag = any reachability or workflow/policy violation reported by the validator after candidate stabilization (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Per‑episode validator traces, repair flags, and scoring reasons were archived (execution/scoring/).

Confirmatory analysis (frozen). The primary confirmatory analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The 2×2 paired contingency compares unsafe_flag between baseline and guarded across pairs and reports discordant pair counts n10 (guarded_only) and n01 (baseline_only), an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent p‑value, and a paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000). Missingness policy (complete_pair_primary) and a one‑attempt retry policy for infrastructure errors were preregistered; the run produced no retriable failures.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run executed as preregistered (execution_manifest): started_at_utc = 2026‑08‑31T13:49:34.191203+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026‑08‑31T14:14:32.660268+00:00. Planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair); hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; cache_hit_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 200. All deterministic consistency checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Thus every shared initial candidate was scored VALID_CONFIGURATION by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in both arms. The paired estimate (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0. The exact two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. The paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI is [0.0,0.0] using bootstrap_seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The zero‑width CI and p = 1.0 are direct arithmetic consequences of complete concordance (no discordant pairs) under the registered estimand and are reproduced exactly in archived analysis artifacts.

Repair and validator diagnostics. repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; repair_provider_trace_path fields are null across scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/). Validator traces per episode record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and final_state snapshots. Representative episodes (task‑000004 through task‑000008) show parsed command counts matching required_command_count and violation_count = 0 with scoring_reason_code = VALID_CONFIGURATION. These per‑episode artifacts substantiate that the validator parsed and validated the shared candidates without generating violations.

Latency and operational notes. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics required a single model call per pair, model_call accounting equals 200. The guarded pipeline added deterministic validator execution time but no repair cycles; execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl record per‑pair timing and show that median additional per‑pair wall time was dominated by deterministic validator evaluation. Exact latency distributions are archived and reproducible from execution/execution_log.jsonl.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. Missingness_summary shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Contamination_summary.csv is empty. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode_accounting_consistent = true and provider call audits passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded interpretation of the degenerate null. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the confirmatory estimand isolates only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates. Observing n11 = 200 (every shared initial candidate valid) implies that, for the chosen LLM (gpt‑5‑mini), the selected synthetic task bank and prompt template family, and the deterministic validator's ruleset, the sampled initial candidates already satisfied the validator constraints; therefore the guarded machinery applied no repairs and changed no acceptance decisions. The archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and execution/scoring/*.json) support this conclusion.

Why the paired bootstrap CI is zero‑width. With no discordant pairs, every bootstrap resample of paired outcomes yields the same paired difference (0.0), producing zero empirical variance and hence a CI [0.0,0.0]. The analysis executor parameters and seed (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000) are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl), showing the CI is a legitimate inferential outcome rather than an analysis error.

Ceiling‑effect contributors (artifact‑supported). The archived manifest and representative tasks indicate three contributors: (1) task‑bank alignment—deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced intents whose required sequences closely match the prompt schema and model output form, increasing the probability of syntactically correct candidates; (2) validator tightness—the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ruleset encoded sequencing and precondition checks used to synthesize reference answers, reducing the chance of discovering violations in this synthetic setting; (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics prevented any guarded‑conditioned regeneration or model variance that might have produced repairs or discordant outcomes. These contributors are evidenced in the task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/* traces.

Design recommendations (artifact‑driven). To permit nondegenerate inference of verifier/gate value we recommend, with direct links to archived artifacts and parameters: (a) increase baseline unsafe rates by augmenting the task generator with adversarial or out‑of‑distribution seeds (the generator's seed and difficulty encoding are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl); (b) change generation semantics to independent generation per condition or multiple independent model samples per condition (this alters the estimand and increases model_call accounting, per execution/model_configuration.json reporting); (c) test multiple model variants or decoding temperatures to reveal model variance (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model and temperature fields); (d) increase automated repair budget and enable iterative repair loops to evaluate repair effectiveness when initial violations appear; and (e) include human‑in‑the‑loop arms to study operator intervention behavior on validator‑flagged candidates. All suggested follow‑ups can be executed by modifying archived manifests and reusing the recorded adapter plumbing.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally limit inference to validator/gate effects and exclude guarded‑conditioned regeneration effects. Construct validity: the binary unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage (sequencing and precondition rules) and may not capture all operational hazards (transient performance regressions, vendor‑specific side effects outside validator rules). External validity: single LLM, single validator, synthetic intents, and sandboxed validation limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, and live device interactions. Conclusion validity: the run was powered to detect ~10 percentage‑point paired reductions per the preregistration plan, but the observed degenerate concordance precludes observing reductions under this sample because baseline unsafe occurrences were absent. Each threat is documented and traceable in the archived preregistration and execution artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing an LLM‑alone observation to the same initial candidate after deterministic verification and bounded automated repair. Every sampled initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator and the guarded pipeline applied no repairs; the paired difference = 0.0 (p = 1.0) with a paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]. This null result is specific to the chosen model (gpt‑5‑mini), the synthetic task bank and deterministic sampling, the validator ruleset, and the shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not contradict prior evidence that validators can reduce unsafe outputs under different experimental regimes (independent per‑condition generation, adversarial inputs, or multiple model samples). We archive full per‑episode and analysis artifacts and recommend follow‑up preregistered designs that increase baseline unsafe rates or permit independent per‑condition generation to quantify verifier/gate contributions under more challenging conditions. All core artifacts and analysis outputs supporting these conclusions are archived and referenced in this manuscript's evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration and autonomy: this study was preregistered as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the execution manifest) and executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Models and tools: single LLM = gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses in execution/model_configuration.json); orchestration/adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Human role and autonomy boundary: the human Research Director selected the topical family and constrained the initial prompt pre‑lock; all literature review, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer‑review emulation, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the lock. Generation semantics clarification: the executed and preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation reused by both arms per pair); therefore the confirmatory estimand measures only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates rather than effects from guarded‑conditioned regeneration or multiple independent model samples. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Key archived artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and the full execution_manifest; preregistration id = autocand_A1_prereg_v1.
limitations: Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics mean baseline and guarded conditions began from an identical initial candidate; the confirmatory estimand therefore measures only validator/repair/gate effects on the same candidate and cannot assess effects of guarded‑conditioned regeneration or prompt engineering.

Construct validity: tasks were synthetic and deterministically selected; the binary unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage (reachability and workflow sequencing rules) and may not capture all operational risks (transient performance regressions, vendor‑specific side effects outside validator rules).

External validity: single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions.

Conclusion validity: the observed null effect (paired difference = 0) reflects this execution's sampling frame in which baseline generation produced only valid candidates; the study was powered to detect ~10 percentage‑point reductions but cannot rule out smaller effects under different sampling or adversarial inputs.
Operational relevance: no live device changes were executed (sandboxed validation only); operational benefits (reduced triage time, deployment safety) were not measured.
Security/contamination: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; no retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) was used, so retrieval‑based poisoning vectors were not evaluated.

Task‑bank reporting: the archived task_manifest.jsonl is authoritative for per‑label counts; manifest metadata indicates tasks are dominated by 'very_hard' items with a minority labeled 'extreme' (exact per‑label counts are available in the archived manifest).
